scope: root-cause fix for the RUN-007 geometry validation gap
command: npm test && node --test src/lib/landfireFuel.test.js && npm run validate:regional-inputs && npm run validate:regional-offline
rootCause1: live GeoServer WCS 1.0.0 legitimately pads/resamples the returned extent to its native grid; confirmed non-negotiable across 4 independently-fetched real samples at different locations/sizes/CONUS regions (bbox -105/-120/-110/-95), resolution up to 1.6x coarser than requested per axis, width/height always exact

It does not prove regional fire-spread accuracy -- it proves the input-contract gate can now actually pass on real data instead of failing closed on everything live.

interpretation: Mean IoU dropped sharply (0.308 -> 0.050) once real, spatially-varying WorldCover fuel and real historical wind/moisture replaced the artificially generous homogeneous TU2/calm baseline -- precision stayed 1.0 while recall collapsed, meaning the model now underpredicts spread extent against real fuel heterogeneity (much of the real land cover is lower-spread-rate or non-burnable relative to blanket TU2). This is NOT a bug and was not tuned away: it is the honest, expected effect of removing an artificially favorable synthetic baseline. It is a real, informative diagnostic result, not evidence of model correctness or incorrectness on its own. Terrain remains synthetic-flat pending the Open-Meteo elevation quota reset (re-run scripts/build-regional-benchmark-fields.mjs tomorrow with no code changes needed).

scope: swap elevation source from quota-limited Open-Meteo to unlimited Copernicus DEM GLO-30 COG; fix a real physics bug real terrain exposed
elevationSourceSwap: Open-Meteo elevation API is itself just a proxy for Copernicus GLO-90 (3x coarser than GLO-30) with a hard daily request quota on the free tier. Replaced with direct windowed reads of the public, unauthenticated Copernicus DEM GLO-30 COG tiles on AWS S3 (same tiling/windowed-read pattern as the existing WorldCover fuel reader) -- no request quota, no auth, finer resolution. All 6 cases: terrain=true, fuel=true, weather=true (6/6 fully real).
bugFound: Enabling real (non-flat) terrain exposed a pre-existing latent bug in src/lib/surfaceSpread.js: the combined wind+slope 'forcing direction' heuristic is a linear vector sum, but wind's alignment response is sub-linear (calculateWindFactor) while slope's is quadratic (calculateSlopeFactor). When wind and slope point in different directions this mismatch let the heuristic's chosen 'head' direction be a real ~2.3% slower than its exact opposite, violating the ellipse transform's required head>=backing invariant (Andrews 2018). Never triggered by 342 prior tests because flat terrain always made slopeRadians=0 exactly, short-circuiting calculateSlopeFactor to 0.
bugFix: src/lib/surfaceSpread.js now computes both the forcing-direction rate and its exact opposite, and labels whichever is larger as head -- fixed at the source (surfaceSpread.js) rather than papering over the fireEllipse.js assertion. No physics formula changed, only which candidate direction is labeled head vs backing.
verification: 343/343 tests pass; validate:rothermel, validate:rothermel:rate, validate:waf, validate:convergence all still pass (bug fix did not disturb equation checks); build clean; validate:hackathon and validate:regional-offline pass, offline validator confirmed zero network access
interpretation: With all three fields real (terrain, fuel, weather), meanIoU is 0.0942 -- higher than the fuel+weather-only intermediate result (0.0497, flat terrain) but still far below the fully-synthetic baseline (0.3085). Precision stayed near 1.0 (0.989) while recall stayed low (0.094): the model consistently underpredicts spread extent against real, heterogeneous conditions rather than overpredicting. This is reported as the honest current diagnostic baseline, not tuned toward any target.

change: Root-caused the recall collapse from RUN-011 (meanIoU 0.0942) via systematic-debugging: (1) instrumented calculateTravelMinutes in firePropagation.js and found fuelPersistenceMinutesByCell was never wired into hackathonBenchmarkRunner.js/build-regional-benchmark-fields.mjs at all (always 0), even though the mechanism exists and is used by the interactive app and Rush Creek replay; (2) found officialBenchmarkFixtures.js modelTimeMinutes was a flat guessed constant (4320 or 1440 min) uncorrelated with each fixture's own already-recorded alarmDate/containmentDate span (oregon-gulch real=14d given 3d; big-five real=138d given 3d; dinely real=4d given 3d; stoll real=0d given 1d, unchanged); (3) while testing a persistence fix, found a genuine solver bug in firePropagation.js calculateTravelMinutes: plannedEndMinutes capped ongoing actively-spreading segments at persistenceDeadline, not just zero-rate waiting segments, making any nonzero persistence value perform worse than none (verified: oregon-gulch raw finiteArrivals dropped 3->1 with persistence=360before the fix, recovered to 3 after).
interpretation: meanIoU improved 0.0942 -> 0.1814 (+92%) from two real, verified bugs, not calibration tuning: a discarded-but-already-computed persistence field, a solver defect that made that field actively harmful once populated, and benchmark time horizons contradicting each fixture's own recorded fire duration. big-five-2015 recall rose 0.13->0.92 (now overpredicts, precision 0.62) once given its real 138-day window. oregon-gulch-2014 barely moved (recall 0.0004->0.0013) and remains unexplained -- its archived 1h dead-fuel moisture has a suspicious single-hour spike (4%->51%->13%) around day 6 not yet root-caused. stoll-2018 (same-day alarm/containment, unrelated cause) and reservoir-2016/deer-2016 (repository fixtures without alarmDate/containmentDate data) were unaffected by these fixes. Still far from a validated regional model; two more open, unexplained low-recall cases remain.

change: Two scoped, user-approved fixes (out of a larger list; spotting/embers, spatial weather, LANDFIRE, live-moisture calibration explicitly deferred as not feasible to do reliably in hackathon time): (1) build-regional-benchmark-fields.mjs sampled Copernicus GLO-30 terrain at a sparse 16x16 grid and bilinearly upsampled to 128x128 despite the source having 400-1000+ native 30m pixels across the case span; changed to sample at native grid resolution (sampleSize=caseDef.size), interpolateElevationGrid becomes an identity pass. (2) Root-caused the oregon-gulch persistence gap further: any actively-spreading edge across a fine, fast fuel (GR2 grass, moisture-of-extinction 15%) that takes longer than about a day to physically cross a cell will straddle a routine ~2-4 hour nightly humidity-driven zero-rate dip, and with zero persistence on non-TL1 fuel that permanently kills the edge regardless of retry timing (verified the Dijkstra solver already retries failed edges from later-arriving neighbors at their own arrival time -- retries were not the missing piece, universal zero persistence was). Added MINIMUM_RESIDUAL_HEAT_PERSISTENCE_MINUTES=240 (4h) as a floor applied to every burnable crosswalk decision in landCoverToFuel.js, representing residual heat along an established flame front bridging a routine diurnal dip -- distinct from and much smaller than the FCCS heavy-fuel duff bridge (up to 48h).
interpretation: meanIoU moved 0.1814 -> 0.1591 (down, not up) with both fixes applied together and real terrain refetched. Per-case: big-five-2015 recall improved 0.92->0.96 but precision fell 0.62->0.52 (more overprediction); dinely-2017 iou fell 0.397->0.333; reservoir-2016 precision collapsed 1.0->0.33 (newly overpredicts slightly) with recall barely moving; oregon-gulch-2014 essentially unchanged (0.0013->0.0013) -- the 4h floor was not enough to bridge its longer effective gaps, or a different cause dominates there; deer-2016 and stoll-2018 unchanged. Both individual fixes are independently justified and verified correct (native-resolution terrain is strictly better-quality input; the persistence floor fixes a demonstrated permanent-failure mechanism), but their combined effect on this 6-case, mostly-tiny-fire benchmark is a net wash to slightly negative in aggregate. Reported as-is, not tuned further to chase a higher number -- consistent with the project rule against tuning on the evaluation set. This is evidence the benchmark's 6 cases (4 of them under 350 acres) are too small/noisy a sample to treat aggregate IoU as a reliable go/no-go signal for either fix in isolation.

change: User pushed back on the RUN-013 regression (fair -- two verified-correct fixes shouldn't just make things worse without an explained mechanism). Isolated the two RUN-013 changes independently: re-ran new-terrain-only (old TL1=360-only persistence) and got meanIoU 0.1591, bit-for-bit identical to the full new-terrain+floor run -- proved the persistence floor changed nothing measurable and the entire regression was attributable to terrain resolution alone (native terrain's real local slope heterogeneity increases false positives/overprediction on the smallest fires -- reservoir precision 1.0->0.33, dinely 1.0->0.96 -- more than it fixes underprediction, net negative on this metric even though the input is objectively higher fidelity). Continuing the search for what IS actually wrong (not just re-litigating what already got fixed), checked the two benchmark cases that were never touched by the modelTimeMinutes fix (RUN-012 only touched officialBenchmarkFixtures.js; reservoir-2016/deer-2016 come from the separate historicalPerimeterFixtures.js) and found the exact same bug pattern again: RESERVOIR_FIRE_2016 has alarmDate 2016-06-26 -> containmentDate 2016-06-30, a real 4-day fire, but hackathonBenchmarkRunner.js's modelTimeMinutes was 1300 (0.9 days) -- under a quarter of the real duration. deer-2016 was already correct (4320 min = 3.00 days, exact match). Fixed reservoir's modelTimeMinutes to 5760 (4 days).
interpretation: reservoir-2016 alone: IoU 0.045->0.210, recall 0.049->0.410 -- a real, large improvement from the same root-cause class already identified (wrong model time horizon), just in a fixture file not covered by the earlier fix. meanIoU 0.159->0.187 (now above the original pre-terrain-fix 0.181) and, more importantly, medianIoU 0.039->0.122 (3x), which is the more honest summary statistic given 4 of 6 cases are still near-zero and one outlier (big-five) dominates the mean. oregon-gulch-2014, deer-2016, and stoll-2018 remain effectively unchanged and unexplained. Do not treat this as a validated model -- it is evidence that a recurring bug class (mismatched model time horizon vs real fire duration) was present in more places than first found, not evidence of general accuracy.

change: Acted on all 3 diagnosed causes from the prior session (wind-cap literature fix, ignition-island avoidance; the 3rd, ERA5 reanalysis understating real gusts, has no responsible fix without a new weather data source and was left as a documented, disclosed limitation rather than faked). (1) Removed the Rothermel 'maximum reliable wind speed' clamp (0.9x reaction intensity) in surfaceSpread.js calculateWindFactor, per Andrews/Cruz/Rothermel 2013 (IJWF 22(7):959-969) which found this original BEHAVE safeguard was an arbitrary, non-empirical limit that under-predicts real wind-driven fire spread, especially for light fuels -- kept a provenance warning instead of a hard cap. (2) Added nearestWellConnectedIgnition() to hackathonBenchmarkRunner.js: when a case has no real public ignition coordinate (only oregon-gulch/big-five/dinely/stoll/reservoir qualify; deer-2016 keeps its real record), BFS-checks the burnable component size at the synthetic bbox-centroid ignition and, if under 25 connected cells, ring-searches outward for the nearest cell with a well-connected component -- avoids starting a fire on an isolated 1-2 cell fuel speck by geometric chance, independent of and without peeking at the observed perimeter.

verification.validateRothermel: pass (BehavePlus TU2 reference points still <5% error)

interpretation: meanIoU 0.187->0.223 (+19%), medianIoU 0.122->0.171 (+40%). stoll-2018 (the case most starved by the wind cap: mean wind 15 km/h, max 22 km/h, yet was stuck at recall 0.03) improved most: recall 0.029->0.137, IoU 0.029->0.136, a direct confirmation the wind-cap fix targeted the right mechanism. dinely-2017 also improved (IoU 0.397->0.441, now precision 1.0). big-five-2015 and reservoir-2016 essentially unchanged (already not wind-cap-limited). oregon-gulch-2014 barely moved (IoU 0.0013->0.0026) -- the ignition-island fix likely did relocate it to a larger connected component (TL1 is 74% of that landscape, not a tiny island once traced further), but the underlying diurnal zero-rate/persistence-floor limitation for fine fuel established in the prior session still dominates there and was not further addressed this run. deer-2016 essentially unchanged (its bottleneck was already identified as the archived weather itself being too calm, which was explicitly left unfixed as not responsibly fixable without a new data source). No physics validator regressed; the wind-cap removal is a published, cited correction, not an invented tuning knob.

change: Built the data-driven persistence fix: replaced the flat 240-min guessed floor with a value computed per-fuel-model from each case's own archived diurnal moisture cycle (longest contiguous run where 1h dead moisture exceeds that fuel's real moisture-of-extinction, capped at 12h so a genuine multi-day wet spell is excluded rather than bridged). Verified HRRR (proposed finer weather source) has zero data coverage for any of our 2014-2018 fire dates before attempting to use it -- confirmed empirically with 2 test API calls, not assumed -- so that fix was correctly abandoned rather than half-built.
interpretation: Computed values are physically sensible and confirm the method works as designed: reservoir-2016/deer-2016/stoll-2018 all measure 0 minutes needed (their archived moisture never exceeds extinction -- matches the earlier direct finding that deer-2016's problem was never the diurnal cycle), oregon-gulch-2014 measures TL1=180min/GR2=420min (a real, larger bridging requirement than the earlier flat 240min guess), big-five-2015 hits the 12h ceiling for every fuel (correctly excluded as a genuine multi-day wet spell, not bridged). Aggregate barely moved (meanIoU 0.223->0.220, medianIoU unchanged) and oregon-gulch-2014 itself barely moved (0.0026->0.0026) despite now having a measured, larger, case-specific persistence budget -- this disproves the hypothesis that the diurnal moisture cycle alone was oregon-gulch's dominant remaining blocker. Something else is capping it that has not yet been isolated. Reported as-is; not a regression (all validators pass), but not the win hoped for either.

change: Found and fixed the last remaining propagation BUG, then completed the structural diagnosis of why the model is unrealistic. BUG: in firePropagation.js calculateTravelMinutes, the ignition-memory budget was implemented as an absolute wall-clock deadline (persistenceDeadline = current.time + persistenceMinutes) but used to bound how long an edge may sit DORMANT waiting for a positive-rate window. Time spent ACTIVELY SPREADING was therefore charged against the waiting budget, so on any edge whose total travel time exceeds the budget the deadline had already expired before the first zero-rate gap was ever reached -- a 250m cell in GR2 grass takes ~2000 min to cross, so no realistic persistence value (240/420 min) could ever engage. Proven by direct experiment before fixing: oregon-gulch cells = 3 at persistence 420, 66 at 5000, 74 at 100000 -- the budget only worked once it exceeded total travel time, which is not what a waiting budget means. Replaced with a cumulative waitedMinutes accumulator charged only during dormant intervals. Also removed a dead-code analytic close-out branch whose condition (!isFinite(boundaryMinutes) && !isFinite(persistenceDeadline)) was unreachable; making it reachable broke WEATHER_POST_WINDOW_POLICY blocking (caught by an existing test), so it was removed rather than kept.
interpretation: oregon-gulch-2014 improved 6x (IoU 0.0026->0.0163) confirming the fix targeted a real mechanism, but remains far from the observed perimeter. meanIoU fell 0.220->0.207 (median unchanged) because big-five-2015 now overpredicts more (recall 1.000, precision 0.402) -- that is the no-suppression limitation being exposed by a longer effective spread window, not a defect in this fix. STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSIS (the actual answer to why the model is unrealistic, independent of any remaining bug): computed the hard physical ceiling per case as peak achievable head rate x model duration. Observed IoU correlates almost perfectly with fire size, not with any code path -- reservoir 153ac/IoU 0.207, stoll 259ac/0.136, big-five 265ac/0.402, dinely 341ac/0.449, deer 1563ac/0.035, oregon-gulch 35111ac/0.016. To match observed area, deer needs 0.329 m/min and oregon-gulch 0.334 m/min sustained OMNIDIRECTIONALLY for the entire duration, but the model's peak head rate (best single moment, best single direction, before ellipse flank/backing reduction) is only 0.363 and 0.288 m/min respectively. Since flank and backing rates run 3-5x below head rate, effective omnidirectional growth is roughly 0.2x peak head rate, leaving large fires 4-6x short in linear extent (60x+ in area). Oregon Gulch is formally impossible even in the degenerate best case: max reachable area 105.8 km2 vs 142.1 km2 observed, assuming uninterrupted peak-rate circular spread. This is not a calibration gap or a bug -- a Rothermel SURFACE fire model structurally cannot generate large-fire growth, which is driven by crown fire, spotting/ember transport, and plume-fire-atmosphere coupling, none of which are implemented. The model is therefore appropriate for small (<400 acre) surface-fire cases and structurally invalid above roughly 1000 acres.

change: Wired up crown fire (Van Wagner 1977 + Rothermel 1991, already built/tested but never connected). Fixed the real persistence bug: persistenceDeadline was an absolute wall-clock deadline from source-cell arrival but was used to bound dormant *waiting* time; active spread time was being charged against it, so on any edge slower than the persistence budget (nearly all of them) the budget was always already expired before the first zero-rate gap -- replaced with a cumulative waitedMinutes accumulator. Found the deeper reason crown fire could never have worked even with canopy data: WorldCover-derived fuel labels every forested cell TL1 (bare compact litter, tops out ~145 kW/m fireline intensity even at 60 km/h wind) while crown initiation needs 168-5300 kW/m; fetched real LANDFIRE FBFM40 fuel and real canopy structure (CH/CC/CBH/CBD) for all 6 cases via curl (Node fetch/undici gets rejected by this USGS server with fake 500s on the byte-identical URL curl succeeds on -- one-time offline freeze script, nothing in the shipped app changed). Fixed an infinite-torching-index guard bug in calculateCrownFractionBurned (RangeError on fuels that can never reach crown initiation intensity). Fixed a severe perf bug: crown-threshold cache key included cell index instead of canopy values, thrashing a 4096-entry cache against 16384 cells; rekeyed on canopy values plus an exact early-out when surface intensity is below crown initiation threshold (~3.8x+ speedup, verified cell counts identical before/after).
interpretation: meanIoU fell 0.207->0.0996 but this is not a regression to chase back: oregon-gulch-2014 (35111 acres, previously proven mathematically impossible for a surface-only model) went 0.016->0.239, now the best case in the suite; deer-2016 (1563 acres) went 0.035->0.145 -- exactly the two fires diagnosed as too large for surface fire alone. Crown fire fixed the mechanism diagnosed as broken. BUT recall shot up everywhere (0.44-0.99) while precision collapsed (0.003-0.53) on the four small fires (152-341 acres) that were fought and contained by firefighters within days on genuinely flammable LANDFIRE fuel -- the model has no suppression mechanism, so it now burns unchecked across real fuel for the whole calendar window. That is the new, correctly diagnosed dominant error source, not a bug in this run. Do not suppress recall or damp crown fire to make the mean look better. Physics validators unaffected (all still pass). Next mechanism: suppression/containment modeling -- suppressionConstraints.js already exists with time-aware barrier support and is accepted by firePropagation.js (suppressionBarrierTimes param, fully wired into the solver's transition-blocking logic), but hackathonBenchmarkRunner.js explicitly reports suppression: 'unavailable' for all 6 benchmark cases -- the engine-side mechanism is real and tested, it is only the benchmark's real-world containment-line/date data source that is missing.

change: Suppression-model data verification (no code changed). Checked whether real dated perimeter-progression data exists for the 6 benchmark fires, per the plan in docs/suppression-data-verification-plan.md, before building any suppression mechanism against hackathonBenchmarkRunner.js.

interpretation: NO-GO on suppression modeling via the two sources checked. The one already-proven-working progression source in this repo (historicalProgressionFixtures.js RUSH_CREEK_PROGRESSION, fetched from apps.fs.usda.gov's EDW_FireOccurrenceAndPerimeter_01 MapServer layer 11/22) is unreachable from this sandbox environment -- this is an environment/network finding, not evidence the data doesn't exist; the same endpoint worked in the session that produced RUSH_CREEK_PROGRESSION. The named fallback (California_fires_since_2014 FeatureServer) is reachable but its schema only carries a single alarm/containment date pair per fire, identical in kind to what officialBenchmarkFixtures.js already has -- it cannot supply the multi-date progression suppression needs, independent of network access. Per the project's standing rule, this is reported as a real NO-GO rather than worked around by substituting alarm/containment dates for observed progression or building on a source proven insufficient. Recommended next action: retry the USDA EDW endpoint from an environment with unrestricted egress (it is known to work, per RUN prior to this one) before concluding suppression is unbuildable; if it remains unreachable, document suppression as a disclosed limitation exactly as HRRR weather resolution was (RUN-016).

interpretation: Primary basis for NO-GO is structural, not connectivity: the California_fires_since_2014 fallback's schema carries only one alarm/containment date pair per fire, identical in kind to what officialBenchmarkFixtures.js already has -- it cannot supply progression data no matter how reliably it can be reached. That finding alone is sufficient for NO-GO and would hold even if USDA EDW came back online tomorrow. Secondary, contingent finding: USDA EDW is unreachable across a genuinely independent path (WebFetch, ECONNRESET) in addition to 4 transport variants and a same-machine retry, all failing identically -- the earlier RUN-019b claim that the same-machine retry constituted "two independent networks" was incorrect (sandbox and retry share the same ISP/router/DNS) and is corrected here; the WebFetch result is what actually establishes independence. Combined verdict unchanged: suppression modeling cannot be validated against real dated perimeter-progression data through either source checked. Recommend documenting "no suppression mechanism, no available progression data source" as a disclosed limitation of this benchmark, exactly as ERA5-vs-HRRR weather resolution was documented in RUN-016, rather than continuing to search for a data source or substituting alarm/containment dates for observed progression. suppressionConstraints.js and firePropagation.js's suppressionBarrierTimes plumbing remain correctly built and unit-tested for future use if a working data source is found later; nothing about the engine-side mechanism needs to change.

change: Benchmark reporting change, not a model change: summarizeHackathonBenchmarks() in hackathonValidation.js now reports results in two tiers alongside (never instead of) the existing aggregate metrics. Tier is derived from observed final area vs a new exported INITIAL_ATTACK_AREA_CEILING_KM2 = 2 km2 (~494 acres): fires below it stayed small because initial attack succeeded, so their perimeter records suppression effort rather than the landscape's capacity to burn. Motivated by RUN-018 (crown fire raised recall everywhere while precision collapsed on exactly the four small contained fires) and RUN-019/019b (no reachable perimeter-progression data source, so suppression is a disclosed limitation rather than a buildable mechanism).

verification.headlineUnchanged: meanIoU 0.0996 / medianIoU unchanged -- existing fields untouched, additive change only, nothing excluded from headline metrics
verification.tierSplit: freeBurningComparable n=2 (deer-2016, oregon-gulch-2014) meanIoU 0.1918 precision 0.2470 recall 0.5930; suppressionConfounded n=4 (reservoir-2016, big-five-2015, dinely-2017, stoll-2018) meanIoU 0.0535 precision 0.1435 recall 0.6790
verification.thresholdProvenance: defined only from observed ground-truth area; does not read model output, so it cannot be tuned to flatter a result. Cross-check: oregon-gulch observed area computes to 142.1 km2, matching the independently-derived figure in RUN-017's structural diagnosis.

interpretation: This is a measurement-validity fix, not a score improvement -- the headline meanIoU is deliberately unchanged at 0.0996 and every case is still scored. What changes is interpretability: on the two fires the model actually attempts to predict (no suppression confound), meanIoU is 0.1918, roughly double the blended figure, while the four suppression-confounded cases sit at 0.0535 and are where precision collapses (0.1435 vs 0.2470). That is the expected signature of a model with no suppression mechanism being scored against fires whose final size was set by firefighters, and it confirms RUN-018's diagnosis quantitatively. Reporting the tiers makes the confound visible rather than letting it silently depress a single aggregate number; it does not remove any case, and the threshold is ground-truth-only by construction so it is not a tuning knob. Future work on spread physics should be judged primarily on the freeBurningComparable tier; movement in the suppressionConfounded tier is largely uninformative about spread until a suppression mechanism exists.

change: Implemented and MEASURED ember/spotting transport, then found it does not help. Added src/lib/spotting.js (three routes tried: an AI-invented loft-height ratio -- rejected; Albini 1979 mechanistic -- dead end because loft height depends on firebrand DIAMETER and no published closed form relates ember diameter to fire intensity, so spot distance FELL with intensity; ELMFire empirical (Lautenberger) E[dX]=a*I^b*U^c with a=5.0,b=0.3,c=0.7,d=250.0 sourced from elmfire docs/user_guide/spotting.rst and cross-checked against build/source/elmfire_spotting.f90 -- monotonic in intensity and wind, operative). Wired into firePropagation.js as deterministic long-range downwind graph edges (never random ignitions; the solver is Dijkstra and all benchmark comparisons depend on determinism), gated behind a flag defaulting OFF. Two variants measured: single landing cell at the expected distance, then multiple deterministic landing cells spanning 0->expected distance.

verification.baselineReproduced: exactly: meanIoU 0.0996, freeBurningComparable 0.1918, suppressionConfounded 0.0535 across two independent runs, confirming the flag defaults off cleanly and the solver stays deterministic

interpretation: NEGATIVE RESULT, reported as-is and not tuned away. Spotting hurts, and the multi-cell 'fix' hurt roughly 3x more than the single-cell version. The diagnostic signal is recall: seeding embers across a full distance range added +0.0009 recall while costing -0.0213 precision -- essentially every spot fire landed where the real fire never went. STRUCTURAL CONCLUSION: this model no longer under-predicts spread, it OVER-predicts it (recall 0.65 vs precision 0.18 means roughly 3.6x too much area burned). Crown fire succeeded because the model was genuinely too small on large fires; that deficit is now closed. Any further spread-ADDING mechanism (spotting, plume coupling) must therefore make accuracy worse until precision improves. The next productive lever constrains spread rather than adding it: suppression (currently blocked -- no reachable perimeter-progression data, RUN-019/019b), model-duration accuracy, or fuel/moisture precision. Spotting wiring is retained but flag-defaults OFF; the module is correct and sourced, it is simply not the binding constraint. Separately discovered and NOT yet fixed: both crown fire and spotting gate on canopyBulkDensityByCell, which only LANDFIRE (US-only) populates, so both mechanisms are silently inert everywhere outside the United States -- and the 6-US-fire benchmark cannot detect this.
